Phase P16 is a batch of user-directed misc fixes surfaced after P15 shipped, grouped into one phase rather than reopening P1/P9/P10/P11/P14.
P16 adds an explicit per-connection preconnect-mode checkbox that overrides P11's settle-window auto-detection.
P16 adds a connection-kind icon picker and a click-to-open connection-error popover.
P16 gives scripts/demo-dbs/ full six-engine coverage.
P16 fixes two font-family bugs and adds testcontainers preset packages for Postgres, MariaDB and Redis.

Each database/queue adapter gets an on-demand compatibility suite, not run in the regular CI/test run, that runs the adapter's existing conformance tests against the oldest and newest server image its Go client library actually supports.
The connection-add UI shows a note per connection kind stating its minimum supported server version.
The compatibility suite exists because development against one pinned test-fixture version never catches version-boundary bugs; it is cheap to build once the adapters are stable.

Studio stores the whole connection URI encrypted (opaque) under cipher scope connection-uri, replacing the refused-keys handling, because sslpassword, tlsCertificateKeyFilePassword and proxyPassword still landed as plaintext in stored URIs on some paths.
Already-stored URIs are not migrated, because nobody else uses the app; old plaintext rows fail loudly, and the stripping code and startup migration were removed.
SecretsRepo.GetURI is the only reader of the stored connection URI, and summaries carry uri: null.
The default view shows the connection URI fully masked and no screen derives display from it; the connection name is what shows.
A Show button decrypts the URI for viewing and editing, reusing the existing password-reveal flow; Save re-encrypts it. Show and Copy URI go through the gated reveal.
P181's acceptance criteria require the URI-encryption decision in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (marked Done); its plan is plans/P181-studio-uri-encryption.md.

The v1.7 M1 local DB MCP server is a new Go MCP server, sibling to internal/repomap, reusing its transport pattern (go-sdk/mcp, loopback-only streamable HTTP) but with its own process, port and tool set.
The DB MCP server's tools are list_connections, list_databases, list_schemas, describe_table and run_query.
The metadata tools (list_databases, list_schemas, describe_table) route through the existing apps/kira-studio/internal/adapters/* layer, with no new metadata path.
run_query executes through the same adapter query path the console UI uses.
The DB MCP server authenticates with a static bearer token with a 7-day expiry that rotates.
Token expiry/rotation is built directly into internal/mcpauth, not a sibling package, so the DB server's token and the repo-map server's token use the same mechanism.
By explicit instruction, the repo-map server's currently non-expiring token gains the identical 7-day rotation, not a second scheme.
A client whose token has lapsed must see a distinct, actionable error, not a generic 401.

The M1 plan designs the rotation trigger (auto-remint on expiry vs. manual remint, and whether it differs between the two servers), plus the DB server's start/stop lifecycle and the storage-root question (share KIRA_HOME with repo-map or use a distinct root).
The DB MCP server is the first phase of the v1.7 chapter: all later phases (permissions, EXPLAIN, Faker, anonymization) extend its tool set or query path, so nothing else can start before it exists.
The DB MCP server implementation lands as part of M1ab.
P212 added a read-only mobile web app (Vue agents module with mobile layout) served by a local web server in Kira Space.
The P212 mobile web scope is three tabs: Backlog, Need You, Plan (narrowed by the user).
The mobileweb server allowlist is GET only plus POST /api/pair.
Mobile web auth (per-device cookie token, csrfGuard, route table) is built so adding a write endpoint takes one route-table row.
The P212 mobile web has no terminal/PTY attach.
First load of the mobile web requires device approval in Kira Space, like the git extension pairing.
The PWA and local CA added in P212 were removed in P223.

The four Settings dialog snapshots in test:visual:space differ because the nav gained a "Mobile access" row. Baselines were not regenerated because of sandbox fonts and must be regenerated on the reference machine.
Design facts for the mobile agents web are in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md under "Mobile agents web (P212, Kira Space)".

The P212 Part 2 amendment plans backlog add and reorder, TUI input for stuck agents, start/next/prev workflow stage, and phone attach of the Claude Code terminal (desktop shows disconnected plus a reconnect button).
P15 part 1 of the request builder UX pass is the presentation half, covering eight of the twelve user-reported items; the editor-behaviour half is split out as P15b.
The response panel, including chrome and pane switcher, is present from the moment a request tab opens, not only after a first send.
A status code's meaning is shown on its own always-visible line, not a truncatable caption plus a hover.
The Studio/Api mode-switch buttons are sized up to the app's own tab metrics and render the icon that modes.ts has declared unused since P1.

.p-input is inline-flex, so a TextField is about 20 characters wide wherever placed unless its call site says otherwise; this is the root cause of the headers/params/form-data table fields not filling their cells and of the URL field never growing.

A new shared Checkbox primitive matching the app's design system replaces all fourteen raw checkbox input call sites app-wide, Studio included, because primitives already live in the shared theme layer (AppButton, TextField, SegmentedControl are precedent).
JSON is promoted to its own top-level body mode as a UI-level promotion over unchanged code+codeLanguage storage, not a new wire/Go/Postman vocabulary and not a data migration.
A body-present indicator on a request's tab is added via a new optional badge() member on the tab-kind registry, which answers what P4 D15 declined.
The toolbar is reflowed so Save sits with the request's name in the view head and the URL field takes the row.
P15 part 1 is sequenced after P12/P13 so it refines a surface already in its final module shape and design-system pass, rather than polishing files about to be renamed or restyled.

P15 is split from P15b because the halves fail differently, P15b opens with a packages/api-core foundation commit unrelated to these eight fixes, and this half touches Studio (nine checkbox call sites and the title bar) so one review pass carries that risk.

The Api module has seven request settings, configurable globally in Settings and per request (overriding the global): httpVersion, requestTimeoutMs, maxResponseMb, sslVerify, followRedirects, maxRedirects, disableCookieJar.
Api setting defaults: HTTP version 2, request timeout 0 (none), max response size 50 MB, SSL verification on, follow redirects on, max redirects 10, disable cookie jar on.
Go's httpclient.Send takes an all-pointer Options struct (nil means default) instead of reading package constants.
resolveSendOptions/orGlobal in bridge/http.go resolve a request's seven null-means-inherit tab-state leaves against the global settings row before every send.
Setting sslVerify to false shows a plain-prose security warning verbatim from the plan, per CLAUDE.md's carve-out for that class of text.
Cookies use one process-wide publicsuffix-keyed cookiejar.Jar, with a throwaway per-send jar for incognito.
Response has SentCookies and ReceivedCookies, taken from the trace's WroteHeaderField hook and every hop's own Set-Cookie.

The request and response Cookies panes reuse one CookiesPane.vue component; request mode shows what the jar would send next (debounced on URL change and after every send), response mode shows sent/received grouped by hop.
Secrets in the new cookie response fields are masked by maskSecrets, with two new loops, like every other response field.
Grow-field sizing bug: the user-agent padding of 2px on the textarea was absent from the sizing replica; fixed by matching it.

A grid item's normal alignment resolves to start, not stretch, for a replaced box with intrinsic size (a textarea via rows), so the grow textarea stayed 1 row tall and scrolled; fixed with align-self: stretch.

The overlay never painted on a grow textarea because the selector input.has-overlay didn't match a textarea; widened to input.has-overlay, textarea.has-overlay, plus line-height: inherit so overlay lines match the textarea's.
The container has no display, so the Playwright ui project is the repo's established substitute for GUI-driven checks.

Setting sslVerify to false shows a plain-prose security warning, taken verbatim from the plan (a CLAUDE.md carve-out for that class of text).
Cookies use one process-wide publicsuffix-keyed cookiejar.Jar, and incognito sends use a throwaway per-send jar.
Response gained SentCookies and ReceivedCookies, built from the trace's WroteHeaderField hook and every hop's own Set-Cookie.

Request and response Cookies panes reuse one CookiesPane.vue component. Request mode shows what the jar would send next, debounced on URL change and after every send. Response mode shows sent/received cookies grouped by hop.
The new cookie fields on the response are secret-masked like every other response field, through two new loops in maskSecrets.
The grow-field textarea had a padding defect: the UA padding of 2px on the textarea was absent from the sizing replica. This was fixed.

A grid item's normal alignment resolves to start, not stretch, for a replaced box with an intrinsic size in that axis (CSS Box Alignment §8.3), and a textarea counts via its rows attribute. Unstretched, the grow textarea stayed 1 row tall and scrolled from row 2, so it needs an explicit align-self: stretch.

The overlay never painted on a grow textarea because the selector .input-wrap input.has-overlay did not match a textarea. It was widened to input.has-overlay, textarea.has-overlay, with line-height: inherit so overlay lines stay aligned with the textarea's past line 2.
The grow-field Playwright test reads line boundaries from the overlay's own Range client rects instead of a hard-coded character count.
The container has no display, so GUI checks in this repo use the Playwright ui project as the established substitute (docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md).
P98 is prep only: it adds shadcn-vue, Tailwind CSS, VueUse, Pinia and TanStack Query as standing dependencies with minimal bootstrap wiring, and migrates no existing .vue file, store or styling.
P98 lands the dependency and convention baseline before P99, so P99 migrates onto libraries already wired and configured instead of doing setup and migration in one pass.

Every future phase's planning pass must adapt its design to lean on the P98-wired libraries (e.g. Tailwind for new UI styling instead of custom CSS) rather than hand-roll equivalents, even where the spec does not say so (CLAUDE.md standing rule).
Every Vue component must be strictly script setup lang="ts" (Composition API only, no Options API).
Pinia stores follow single responsibility: one store per concern, never a grab-bag app-wide store.
P98 added pinia 4.0.3, @tanstack/vue-query 5.103.2 and @vueuse/core 15.0.0 to the root package.json, matching the monaco-editor/slickgrid precedent; VueUse needs no bootstrap step.
state/pinia.ts exports the single createPinia() instance and state/queryClient.ts exports the single QueryClient; main.ts registers both plugins before directive/mount.
The QueryClient uses retry: false and refetchOnWindowFocus: false because every query resolves over the Wails bridge to the local Go process, never the network.
The @ alias maps to ./src in both vite.config.ts resolve.alias and tsconfig.json compilerOptions.paths; existing source keeps relative imports and @/ is for shadcn-vue's generated import specifiers.

shadcn-vue is configured with reka-ui base, nova style, neutral base color, lucide icons and CSS variables, via components.json, src/lib/utils.ts and src/theme/shadcn-bridge.css; no components were generated (P99's scope).
shadcn-bridge.css maps every shadcn-vue variable to an existing --kira-* token and has no .dark block, because tokens.css is a single :root and index.html hardcodes class="dark".
base.css imports shadcn-bridge.css after ./vscode-bridge.css.
knip.json has ignoreDependencies entries for @vueuse/core, reka-ui, class-variance-authority, tw-animate-css, @lucide/vue, clsx and tailwind-merge, plus a workspace ignore for src/lib/utils.ts.
The icon dependency is @lucide/vue 1.47.0, not lucide-vue-next, as named by the shadcn-vue registry for the lucide icon library under this style.
src/lib/utils.ts uses a single combined clsx import and an explicit : string return type on cn().
The shadcn-vue 2.8.2 CLI does not support --dry-run, --diff or --view.
Never unset HTTPS_PROXY to work around a tool's network failure, because docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md says this is never the fix.

shadcn-vue 2.8.2 init fails with 'TypeError: fetch failed' under Bun and Node 22 because ofetch passes an undici ProxyAgent to the runtime's global fetch; the same endpoints work via curl or bare fetch.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Stack table has a row for the frontend library baseline (Vue/Vite/Tailwind v4/shadcn-vue on Reka/Pinia/TanStack Query/VueUse); P99 migrates the existing 39 reactive() modules and 200 .vue files onto them.

P131 Part 2 moves packages/git-ui's App.vue and every non-dialog, non-review components/*.vue (including WorktreeList.vue's own dialog and FileTree.vue) onto shadcn-vue; the only kira-ui import allowed to remain is KuiColumnResizeHandle (used in App.vue and CommitGrid.vue).
The plan for P131 Part 2 is docs/v2.0/plans/P131-part2-git-graph.md; it keeps Part 2 as one continuous, order-dependent chain with no split.
git-ui owns its own helpers lib/cn.ts, lib/rowVariants.ts and lib/menuModel.ts (menuModel.test.ts moved there) instead of importing them from kira-ui.
badgeVariants lives in badgeClass.ts, a .vue-free module in the theme package. REF_BADGE_CLASS and refBadgeClass live in refBadges.ts, also .vue-free, so bun test can run them.

AttributeTooltip and TooltipAnchorBridge were hoisted from workbench into packages/theme/src/components/; workbench/src/state/tooltip.ts and the workbench AttributeTooltip.vue were deleted, nothing references them, and Studio's SlickGridHost.vue import was updated.
The grid tooltip attribute is data-kira-tip (was data-kui-tip), and AttributeTooltip also opens on keyboard focus. It is wired in CommitGrid.vue, CommitMeta.vue, FileTree.vue and BranchPicker.vue.
git-ui's mount() wraps both roots in a TooltipProvider via the new MountRoot.vue.

Row context menus and the point-anchored DropdownMenuContent (RowContextMenu.vue) use prioritize-position, because reka's Popper runs shift before flip by default and shift alone clamps a 0×0 point anchor's overflow to zero, starving flip of a signal.
In App.vue, onClickOutside takes a third argument ignoring '[data-reka-popper-content-wrapper]' so the force-delete Popover's outside-click does not trigger the detail-region's dismiss handler.
The force-delete confirmation is now a reka Popover and dismisses on outside-click or Escape, which the old hand-rolled popup never did.

packages/git-ui/src/theme/app-shell.css was deleted (including its raw-checkbox rule) and main.ts no longer imports it. No raw form controls (input, select, textarea, checkbox) remain in git-ui's App.vue and components.
Webview test selectors were moved from kira-ui surfaces (kui-segmented-badge, kui-tooltip, data-kui-tip) onto reka surfaces, including floating-geometry.spec.ts.

Acceptance for P131 Part 2 requires test:ui:space, test:webview, test:unit and test:ui:studio green, and the graph shown live in both hosts; test:ui:studio runs because Studio's SlickGridHost.vue import changed.

In a shared checkout, commit with an explicit pathspec (git commit -m msg -- files), never git add -A or git add ., and stash with a pathspec rather than bare git stash, so other sessions' concurrent edits are not bundled or lost.

In git-ui's main.ts, the remaining kira-ui residue is the vKuiTooltip import, the 'kui-tooltip' directive registration and the kui-bridge.css import. Review still uses the directive until Part 3 moves it off kira-ui.
git-ui adds no wrapper layer over shadcn components: no defineComponent in scope, no non-setup script blocks, and no Git*Button-style wrapper files.
RowContextMenu's contextmenu listener is on RowActionsButton, not on the row's checkout button, so tests must right-click the row's "More actions" button.
In search, the first Escape dismisses the dropdown but keeps the query, and the second Escape clears the query and closes the search.
fakeGraphHost.ts's harness does not vary --vscode-* variables between body.vscode-dark and body.vscode-light, so identical computed colors in both themes are expected.

Sandbox worker contention causes timing-flake boot timeouts in the Playwright UI suites (test:ui:space, test:ui:studio), as documented in CLAUDE.md and DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md. Re-running the failing tests with --workers=1 passes.
apps/kira-studio/frontend has no dependency on @kira/git-ui.

fakeGraphHost.ts's fixture never sets capabilities.write in its app.init response, so write-gated UI (inline rename, worktree-remove dialog, gated on actions?.capabilities.write in App.vue/BranchPicker.vue) is unreachable from it.

fakeGraphHost.ts never mocks commit.detail (only fakeReviewHost.ts does, for the /review route), so DetailState.detail never resolves on /graph and CommitMeta/FileTree content gated by v-if="detail" never mounts there. commit-meta-clamp.spec.ts therefore uses its own commitMetaHarnessServer.ts mount.
In Kira Space tests, installGitStreamMock's extraResults can mock commit.detail, so the detail pane shows real CommitMeta content.

The minimal refs.list fixture in graphStreamFixture.ts renders zero .kv-badge elements, so App.vue's branch-tip-to-badge overlay needs more than that fixture wires; ref badges are covered by graph-columns.spec.ts's 'ref/tag badges render as outlines' test.

The search toggle Button's color resolves to rgb(204, 204, 204) in the VS Code webview (--kv-* bridged) and rgb(157, 157, 157) in Kira Space (unprefixed --kira-* root); the two hosts' token tables are intentionally distinct, confirming the two-root split.

A standalone Playwright config outside the repo's test trees cannot resolve @playwright/test's module graph, so scratch specs must be placed temporarily inside apps/kira-space-vscode/tests/interaction/ or apps/kira-space/tests/ui/.
